To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the financial centre of Frankfurt will remain an important location for financial activities.
Frankfurt is a financial centre of global relevance, but its future role is uncertain.
Frankfurt is a financial centre that is well positioned to profit from the development of financial technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how ICT affects the spatial organisation of financial services.
the following questions: What are the implications of ICT for the spatial organisation of the financial industry, in particular for the Frankfurt financial centre?
the following questions: How can ICT be used to reorganise financial services?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the value chain approach provides a useful framework for analysing the spatial (re)configuration of the financial industry and the impact of ICT on financial services.
Frankfurt is not only a ‘traditional’ financial centre but also a ‘new’ financial centre, which combines the traditional with the new.
the Frankfurt financial centre will remain a significant location for the financial industry, but its role in the global network of financial services will change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the financial centre in Germany has to be understood as an agglomeration with a strong focus on Frankfurt, but also including other locations.
Frankfurt’s role as a financial centre has changed in the past years.

the financial industry in Frankfurt will remain a major player in global finance, and that Frankfurt will continue to attract financial firms, especially those with a strong focus on technology and innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICT is not a substitute for proximity.
Frankfurt will remain an important location in Europe, although its position may change as a result of the implementation of new ICT.
ICT does not necessarily imply the relocation of functions to low wage centres, but rather a re–bundling of functions among financial services centres.
